newsitem.title: USA: US SEC says ex-bond trader made fake diary entries.
newsitem.headline: US SEC says ex-bond trader made fake diary entries.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is accusing former bond trader Joseph Jett of entering false information in his diary, which was used in a trial last year.

In a brief submitted Wednesday for its administrative case against Jett, the SEC accused Jett of manipulating entry dates after his employment with Kidder, Peabody & Co was terminated and as the SEC and others began investigating his trading activities.

"Jett's diary would not have been admissible under the Federal Rules of Evidence because it is not authentic," the agency wrote in its brief. The SEC restated its allegations that Jett created millions of dollars in phony profits to hide Kidder's trading losses.

The agency last Spring in administrative hearings for the case made similar assertions, citing many inconsistencies between his personal diary and a separate diary kept on his secretary's computer. The agency then called the diary "highly suspect evidence."

But Jett has maintained that the diary in his personal computer contained critical remarks about his bosses as well as personal observations about other Kidder employess. He said he transferred the diary to a Kidder computer used by his secretary, but omitted any personal remarks from the version given to the secretary.

The SEC in its latest brief, which may be its last written word before an SEC administrative law judge issues a ruling, alleged that Jett had the opportunity to manipulate the diary and that entries in both his personal computer and the diary entries in his secretary's computer do not match.
"After Jett was terminated by Kidder, Jett had possession and control of the Jett diary for at least three weeks," the agency said.
The said SEC in the brief that it issued a subpoena for the diary on May 12, 1994 but did not receive a copy from Jett until February 1996.

"While Jett would like the court to believe that the Jett diary was a contemporaneous record of events that occurred while he was employed at Kidder, the evidence does not support this contention," the agency said.
